newsitem.title: USA: Warm days, little rain in Florida citrus belt-FASS.
newsitem.headline: Warm days, little rain in Florida citrus belt-FASS.

text.p: Warm days, cool nights and very little rain typified the weather this week in the Florida citrus belt, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS), said.

According to FASS, those trees that had lost foliage due to freezing temperatures and frost on January 19 are showing signs of new growth. Picking crews are rapidly moving any damaged fruit to the processors.
Caretakers in the area are discing and cutting dead cover crops for fire prevention.
FASS reported an estimated 217,000 boxes of navel oranges were harvested in the week ended February 2, up from 180,000 boxes the previous week and 266,000 boxes in the week ended January 19.
An estimated 10,214,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended February 2, up from 7,308,000
boxes the prior week and 11,053,000 boxes the week ended January 19, FASS said.
